display_name: The drink-driving alcohol thresholds of Israel's Traffic Ordinance s.64B(a) and Traffic Regulations reg. 169A, on L4's rule-effective-time axis -- one rule, two vintages, Amendment No. 97 of 2010 in between

language.note: Body text, identifiers and the @nlg heralds are English. The binary this was checked on (l4-ide unstable-20260907) predates `@lang` and `l4 nlg --lang`, so the heralds are not language-tagged; a Hebrew-canonical twin row, encodings/legalese-he/, carries the same encoding with Hebrew identifiers, section titles and heralds. Both rows are hand-written; source/twin-check.py proves them token-for-token identical through encodings/legalese-he/glossary.json, and check.sh proves they answer identically. This row is the oracle.

scope: Traffic Ordinance s.64B(a), the definition of 'intoxicated' (שיכור), paragraphs (3) (the Minister's threshold) and (3A) (the 50 microgram / 10 milligram threshold for a new driver, a driver under 24, a driver of a commercial or work vehicle over 3,500 kg, and a driver of a public vehicle, inserted by Amendment No. 97, S.H. 2265 p. 91, published 9 December 2010); s.62(3), the offence of being intoxicated while driving on a road or in a public place; Traffic Regulations reg. 169A, the definition of 'alcohol concentration in the body' (240 micrograms per litre of exhaled air / 50 milligrams per 100 millilitres of blood, as inserted by K.T. 6825 p. 114, 10 November 2009). The threshold is a function of RULES EFFECTIVE DATE; the encoding covers rules-effective dates from 10 November 2009 and returns an explicit 'not encoded' value before that. NOT encoded: paragraphs (1), (2) and (4) of the definition; the three-hour presumption in paragraph (3); the sampling powers of s.64B(a1)-(o); the 'person in charge of the vehicle' limb of s.62(3); s.12A (who is a new driver: an input); the penalty; the general threshold before 10 November 2009. Text as at the Wikisource revisions of 2026-09-09 deposited in source/.

not_reviewed.note: No human who knows Israeli traffic law has read this against the statute. The paragraph (3A) text was read against the deposited gazette issue of Amendment 97 and found identical to the consolidated Wikisource text; reg. 169A was read against the deposited K.T. 6825.

forks.F1: Amendment 97's commencement is taken as its publication day, 9 December 2010, because the Act has no commencement clause; the default rule's current statutory home was not pinned (NOTES.md section 4). Roznai's 'November 2010' is the adoption date, 29 November 2010.
forks.F2: The general threshold before 10 November 2009 (the Regulations' former 'המידה הקבועה') is not established: the 1982 gazette is an image-only scan. The encoding returns 'the text in force on that date is not encoded' rather than assuming 240/50.
forks.F3: 'A driver who has not yet turned 24' is modelled as an age-in-years input compared with 24, not as date-of-birth arithmetic against the day of the sample.
forks.F4: New-driver status (s.12A) is an input; the two-year period and its extensions are not derived.
forks.F5: Every 'exceeds' (העולה על / עולה על) is strict: a reading exactly at 50, 10, 240 or 50, and a vehicle of exactly 3,500 kg, are not over the figure.
